- Earned ribbon classes remain visible after an award is promoted. Medal details and inspection show the selected class's corresponding ribbon and devices. Visible artwork determines mounted-medal scale.
- Click an operations-room ribbon to open its medal wall. The battlefield decoration picker uses smooth scrolling and consumes wheel input; it no longer changes camera zoom.

Do not use GitHub's automatic **Source code** archives to play. See **START-HERE.txt** for the exact required files and **SHA256SUMS.txt** for download checksums.

## Orders from the Front

- **A new Western Front operations map.** Zoom and pan through the campaign, compare assignments and inspect both commanders, orders, terrain, expected opposition and incoming attachments.
- **Four historical campaign forks.** Choose between paired assignments at Bullecourt/Messines, Langemarck/Menin Road, the Lys/Villers-Bretonneux and Selle/Valenciennes. A new campaign follows sixteen operations through each army's twenty-operation roster. Victory commits the branch; defeat leaves the choice open. Completed assignments remain replayable.
- **Dispatches with tangible consequences.** Accept an attached section for the coming battle without spending the normal recruitment cycle, or send it to another formation and retain research points. Replaying or switching assignments cannot duplicate the reward.
- **Connected British and German stories.** Revised orders link Arras, Flanders, Cambrai, the spring crisis and the Hundred Days, with generated period-scene reconstructions and distinct armistice epilogues.

## Company tactics

- Reinforcements reach the field edge in about three seconds. Combat continues into the rear approaches, and a breakthrough requires clearing the opposing rear guard.
- Gold and silver command stars make leadership effects visible. Nearby NCOs provide a 25% relative accuracy bonus, rising to 50% after commissioning. Bonuses do not stack; leaders halt behind their rifle escorts.
- Research unlocks **FIXED / MOBILE** organisations in the same machine-gun slot. Fixed sections retain longer reach and stronger suppression; four-man mobile sections move faster and deploy or pack 30% faster. Both require supported firing positions and share recruitment readiness. Switching leaves deployed troops unchanged.
- Observation training belongs to command sections rather than a separate recruitment card. Settled, escorted commanders with clear sight improve the first field-gun or mortar salvo; movement, smoke and heavy suppression interrupt correction.
- Marksmen are more effective against visible machine-gun crews. Four-man pioneers prepare sooner and approach obstacles only when clearance is needed on their route. Machine-gun escorts are steadier around deployed weapons.
- Ordinary research depends on points and prerequisites, allowing preparation before an attachment arrives. Historically late weapons retain date restrictions. Researched respirators are limited to assault, pioneer and flamethrower sections, take time to don, and reduce gas exposure rather than making it harmless.

## Ground, water and atmosphere

- More varied trench layouts, chalk slopes, broken ridges, flooded approaches, canals, railway cuttings, ruins and winter ground, with operation-specific weather and new distant landscapes.
- Shell holes and standing water extend through the central crossing. The distant earth shares the fighting ground's material response, with revised wet-mud shading and blends for chalk, debris and snow.
- Rain and incoming ordnance disturb actual crater pools; heavier blasts stir suspended mud. Settled bullet and blast casualties bleed into connected water. Dark deposits spread and dilute within the shoreline while reflections remain visible. This uses a bounded real-time approximation, not a full fluid-volume simulation.
- More varied victory group calls and answering whistles, followed by the instrumental score.

## Progression and fixes

- Winning no longer reveals next-operation troop or support cards during the victory outro or result screen. Availability stays with the completed battle until the next preparation. Introductions cover attachment dates skipped by campaign branches.
- Existing victories, paid research and settings are retained. Older mobile-gun and observation selections migrate into the machine-gun and command slots without granting free research. Existing acknowledged dispatches receive no duplicate reward.

## Compatibility and updating

Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11 x64, with current graphics drivers. **Play.cmd** uses DirectX 12; **Low Spec.cmd** supplies the DirectX 11 Low-quality fallback, and **Safe Mode.cmd** supplies a DirectX 12 SDR troubleshooting mode. Required Microsoft x64 runtime files and third-party notices are included.

English is the default interface language; Chinese is available in Settings. Battlefield voices remain English and German. HDR and NVIDIA DLSS, Ray Reconstruction and Frame Generation depend on compatible hardware. See the [README](https://github.com/ShoWTimETheKey/Warfare-Front#graphics-and-requirements) for requirements and quality presets.

Extract updates into a new folder and keep the complete extracted folder together. Existing campaign saves and normal settings remain in your Windows user profile. The game runs offline; its optional online update check opens the release page without automatically installing anything.

The exact V53 Shipping build passed 40 focused checks and six captured scenes received visual review. This is targeted validation, not testing on every computer or a new performance guarantee. The package contains the finished game and required notices, without development projects, old builds, private reports or player saves.

Warfare Front is an independent historical game, not an official Armor Games or Warfare 1917 / Warfare 1944 release. Generated archival-style images are period reconstructions, not authentic historical photographs. Redistribution is governed by the complete package's licence and notices.

The download EXE extracts the numbered volumes; it is not the game or a downloader. No installed 7-Zip, Unreal Engine, Epic Games Launcher, development tools or game account are required. **Do not download GitHub's automatic Source code archives to play.**

## V49 — Breakthrough and the Rear Guard

A section slipping past a defending soldier no longer wins a territory victory simply because its average position reaches the end of the map.

- The breakthrough line lies deeper in the opposing rear. **Every surviving member of the advancing section** must cross; a vehicle must carry its **whole hull** across.
- Active defenders in the last trench and rear approaches contest the objective, including operational enemy armour. Corpses, wrecks, off-map reserves and enemies elsewhere do not obstruct a valid breakthrough.
- Infantry and tanks can respond to a visible rear guard they have passed inside the final defensive sector. Weapon range, terrain and smoke still govern engagement.
- Stationary tanks recheck the objective when accompanying infantry clear the remaining defenders. English and Chinese objective guidance explains the revised conditions.
- Morale victory remains a separate way to end a battle.

## Also new since the previous public release, V43

### Infantry and armour

- Corrected opposing tanks losing their engagement when routes brought them alongside or past one another. Hull turning, weapon traverse, elevation and muzzle clearance govern fire; the machine-gun-only Whippet does not gain an ahistorical anti-tank cannon.
- Stabilized anti-tank rifle deployment and reloading to prevent repeated prone/standing transitions caused by a moving weapon muzzle.
- Corrected machine-gun assistants retaining running poses beside deployed weapons, crew reformation and pioneer approach movement. Trench positions now follow the curved works with shoulder clearance.
- Machine-gun accuracy increased by 15%, with firing and contact ranges reduced by 15%. Rifle-armed companions retain their own weapon profiles.
- Rifle-grenade section recruitment prepares 30% faster, with 20% wider grenade dispersion; weapon reload speed is unchanged. Anti-tank rifle preparation time is reduced by 30%; flamethrower preparation time by 15%.
- The flamethrower operator survives the first landed firearm round; a second is fatal, with no regeneration. Explosions remain lethal on a successful hit, and accompanying riflemen retain their existing rules.

### The battlefield

- Rebuilt operation-specific wet clay, mud, shell scars and flooded depressions, with shared water levels and continuous wet margins. Revised scan detail, texture streaming, roughness and overcast lighting improve surface definition.
- Corrected discontinuities in ground blending and shading. Separate water geometry replaces painted reflective patches; water uses depth-dependent colour and irregular surface ripples.
- Extended the rear landscape toward the distant battlefield while retaining the alignment of firing steps, railway supports and unit footing.
- Replaced static smoke shapes with evolving volumetric sequences, rolling pockets and internal shadow. Gas remains lower than screening smoke.
- Separated explosion flash, directional soil ejection, smoke and settling dust, with distinct grenade, mortar and shell scales. Shared effects are prepared during operation loading, and Low, Medium and High retain separate effects budgets.

### Campaign and presentation

- Shorter early and middle operations, with more space between three active trenches; the final two operations retain five trenches and their longer depth.
- Both twenty-operation campaigns have faction-specific tactical context. Unit, support and research descriptions combine historical flavour with practical strengths, limitations and upgrade effects.
- Mirrored morale labels, revised Chinese typography and clearer objective guidance. Primary battle-console labels remain English in either interface language; Chinese tooltips and descriptions remain localized.
- Faster bullet-fatality falls, staggered victory and surrender reactions, revised faction-specific victory crowds and recorded whistle accents. Cause-dependent casualty calls retain battlefield spacing and separate voice/music controls.

## Compatibility and updating

- Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11, 64-bit, with current graphics drivers. Normal launch uses DirectX 12; **Low Spec.cmd** provides a 720p DirectX 11 / Low-quality fallback. **Safe Mode.cmd** provides a 1080p DirectX 12 SDR troubleshooting mode.
- English is the default interface language; Chinese is available in Settings. Battlefield voices remain English and German.
- HDR and NVIDIA DLSS, Ray Reconstruction and Frame Generation are optional and require compatible hardware. See the [README](https://github.com/ShoWTimETheKey/Warfare-Front#graphics-and-requirements) for quality presets and requirements. Performance depends on hardware and settings; this release has not been physically tested on every target GPU.
- Extract this version into a **new folder**. Existing campaign saves and normal display preferences are retained. The game runs offline. The optional update check compares versions online and lets you open the release page; it does not download or install updates.

The relocated Shipping build passed focused rear-guard and breakthrough regression checks. title: Warfare Front V37 — Eyes over the Battlefield
notes:

## Reconnaissance with a purpose

- Both armies can use an actual reconnaissance pass to obtain a temporary report of visible infantry, machine guns and tanks in the photographed sector. The report and practical guidance appear in the patrol's existing hover panel.
- Indirect fire ordered into a clear, reported sector scatters less and arrives sooner. Aerial-liaison research extends the report's useful life.
- Reports describe what the aircraft observed on that pass. They do not track hidden movement or reveal later reinforcements. Terrain and smoke affect observation, and fresh smoke can prevent registration.
- Enemy aerial observation follows the same visibility rules. Air-support decisions use the difficulty-dependent observation and coordination delays.

## Heavier, more responsive support

- Field guns and mortars now deliver four salvos; creeping barrages deliver six. Bombing, antitank fire, strafing, smoke and gas carry more ammunition or replenishing emissions.
- Support response times are slightly shorter across the board. Antitank guns respond more quickly when an observed target and a clear firing line are available.
- Strafing uses two focused, overlapping firing lanes with less random lateral spray. Damage now arrives with the visible tracer.
- Bomb targets and release timings are committed when the run is ordered. Later commands cannot redirect airborne ordnance.
- Smoke screens last longer, with clearer guidance on obscuring direct fire and protecting movement. Gas also persists longer. Ordered fire remains dangerous to friendly troops entering its path.

## Armour and battlefield movement

- Tanks enter along several lateral routes and turn around disabled vehicles and wrecks, with clearance based on the actual hull orientation. Immobilised tanks no longer consume the mobile tank allowance.
- Tracks withstand more punishment, and general explosive blasts are less effective against them. Track motion follows the distance actually travelled.
- Infantry can attempt an inaccurate, animated grenade throw towards a nearby tank's hull. Only very close detonations have a limited chance of damaging running gear or, more rarely, the hull; ordinary grenades remain poor antitank weapons.
- All four tank models gain varied period-format identification markings and revised paint, dust, rust, camouflage and exposed-metal treatment. These are original composite crew assignments, not claims to reproduce particular historical vehicles exactly.
- Operations have slightly less battlefield depth, bringing the opposing lines closer and reducing uneventful travel.

- Unit and support descriptions remain readable while the item is cooling down, with readiness shown separately. Reconnaissance reports and guidance are available in English and Chinese.
- Later operations now use appropriate painted portraits of Henry Horne, Otto von Below, Adolph von Carlowitz and Bruno von Mudra. Existing commanders retain consistent portraits across their appearances, with correctly proportioned crops and room for their biographies.
- Repeated confirmation during preparation can no longer restart loading or reopen an introduction card over it. Optional background streaming no longer produces a false loading failure after the battlefield is ready.
- The battlefield receives a short rendering warm-up before play begins. Archival-style photo transitions are reserved for major campaign moments; ordinary page changes use shorter fades. Missing transition images no longer leave an opaque screen over the destination.
